div.div: ذَاتِ الحُبْكِ and الحِبْكِ and الحَبَكِ and الحُبَكِ and الحُبُكِ and الحُبِكِ (TA) and الحِبَكِ (Bd in li. 7] and الحِبُكِ and الحِبِكِ (TA) are various readings in the Kur [li. 7]: الحُبْك is a contraction of الحُبُك, of the dial. of Benoo-Temeem: الحِبْك is a contraction of الحِبِك: الحَبَك is as though its sing., or n. un., were حَبَكَةٌ: الحُبَك is as though its sing. were حُبْكَةٌ: الحُبُك is the common reading, and is pl. of حِبَاكٌ [q. v.] or of حَبِيكَةٌ: الحُبِك is of a form unused [in any other instance]: (TA:) الحِبَك is like النِّعَم [as though its sing. were حِبْكَةٌ]: (Bd:) الحِبُك is affirmed to be a mixture of two dial. vars.: الحِبِك is of a rare measure, like إِبِلٌ &c. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
